package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, distributed via Linux repos and bundled in proprietary products)
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a high-severity Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input, causing the library to resolve attacker-controlled URIs. This can be exploited to access internal resources, perform denial of service, or chain with other vulnerabilities for unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is present by default in affected versions and can be triggered without authentication, making the entire package version range dangerous in security-sensitive contexts.

execution_context.file_location: XML parsing logic in xmltooling library (e.g., KeyInfo element processing)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the application parses attacker-supplied XML, the code resolves the URI in the KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod element, causing the server to make an HTTP request to an attacker-controlled domain, potentially accessing internal resources or exfiltrating data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing untrusted XML input to trigger arbitrary network requests from the server is a classic SSRF pattern, enabling attackers to pivot into internal networks or abuse the server as a proxy.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal XML signature/key processing should only resolve trusted, whitelisted URIs or local resources, not arbitrary attacker-supplied URLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In some SAML/crypto workflows, remote key retrieval is legitimate if restricted to trusted endpoints.
key_indicators: Unrestricted URI resolution from XML input
No authentication required to trigger network requests
Use of KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod with attacker-controlled URI

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits crafted SAML/XML input with a malicious KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod URI.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and makes a server-side request to the attacker-controlled URI.

attack_chain.action: The server-side request can access internal resources, exfiltrate data, or be chained with other vulnerabilities (e.g., command injection) for further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential denial of service, internal network access, or unauthenticated remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: XML input containing KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with external (non-whitelisted) URIs
Unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests triggered during XML/SAML processing
Resolution of attacker-controlled URIs during SAML authentication or XML signature validation
file_indicators: Presence of xmltooling library versions prior to 3.2.4
Application logs showing parsing of SAML/XML with external KeyInfo URIs
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to untrusted or attacker-controlled domains from SAML/XML processing endpoints
Requests to internal network resources (e.g., 169.254.169.254, localhost) triggered by SAML/XML input
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for SAML/XML input containing KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements with external or untrusted URIs. Detect unexpected outbound network requests from authentication or XML processing services, especially during SAML assertion handling. Audit application dependencies for vulnerable xmltooling versions and upgrade to 3.2.4 or later. Use web application firewalls or XML schema validation to block or sanitize untrusted URIs in XML input.
